title: The relative Cech nerve is one-coskeletal
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:F\to G$ be a morphism of presheaves of sets, that is, functors $\mathcal C^{op}\to\mathrm{Set}$. Form the simplicial presheaf $E$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] with $E_q=F\times_G\cdots\times_G F$ ($q+1$ factors), faces deleting factors and degeneracies repeating factors; its augmentation to the constant simplicial presheaf $G$ is the common image under $f$. Then $E$ is $1$-coskeletal: its canonical map $E\to\operatorname{cosk}_1\mathrm{sk}_1E$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] is an isomorphism. More precisely, for every simplicial presheaf $T$, restriction gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(T,E)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\mathrm{sk}_1T,\mathrm{sk}_1E)$, and both sets identify with $\{g:T_0\to F\mid fgd_0=fgd_1:T_1\to G\}$. In particular, if $a:T\to G$ is an augmentation and $g:T_0\to F$ satisfies $fg=a_0$, it determines a unique simplicial map $T\to E$ with degree-zero map $g$; its degree-$q$ map is the tuple of $g$ applied to the $q+1$ vertices, and this map commutes with the augmentations to $G$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 018I, label lemma-cosk-minus-one, including the displayed morphism bijection and its vertex-tuple construction. Applied to the presheaf category, which has objectwise fibre products.
